newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-PSG PENALISED BY UEFA AFTER STEAUA MATCH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PSG PENALISED BY UEFA AFTER STEAUA MATCH.

text.p: Paris St Germain said they have been stripped of two crucial away goals for fielding a suspended player against Steaua Bucharest of Romania in a European Cup preliminary round first-leg match last week.
A PSG spokesman said on Monday that European soccer's ruling body UEFA had changed the club's 3-2 defeat in Bucharest to a 3-0 loss after ruling that defender Laurent Fournier should not have played.
Fournier, who played the whole match, was ineligible because of bookings from last season. Bucharest appealed against his presence to UEFA.
The punishment means that PSG, French league runners-up last season, will have to win by at least four clear goals in the return match in Paris on August 27.
Failure will mean a financially disastrous elimination from the lucrative Champions' league.
The spokesman said Claude Le Roy, the Paris club's sporting director, had said that his players nevertheless remained "confident" that they could still qualify.
